title: DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling
abstract: arXiv:2610.04933v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Scaling robot data and model capacity has improved Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, but further progress is constrained by the high cost of robotic data. Verifier-guided test-time scaling offers an efficient alternative by sampling multiple action candidates and selecting the one most likely to lead to task success at inference time. Existing classification-based verifiers learn from trajectory-level outcomes but treat all visited states equally, even though their value for candidate discrimination can vary across a trajectory. At many states, plausible actions are similar and provide limited discrimination signal, while only a sparse set of decision-critical states admits meaningfully different actions that can substantially affect downstream outcomes. translated_title: DiVeR：面向VLA测试时扩展的决策关键验证器学习
translated_abstract: 扩展机器人数据规模和模型容量已经提升了视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略的性能，但进一步的进展受到机器人数据高昂成本的制约。基于验证器引导的测试时扩展提供了一种高效的替代方案，它在推理时采样多个动作候选，并选择最有可能导向任务成功的那一个。现有的基于分类的验证器从轨迹级别的结果中学习，但对所有访问过的状态一视同仁，尽管它们对候选动作的区分价值在轨迹中各不相同。在许多状态下，合理的动作彼此相似，只能提供有限的区分信号；而只有稀疏的一组决策关键状态才允许存在实质性不同的动作，并能够显著影响下游结果。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了DiVeR，它通过采样动作表示的分散程度来估计决策关键性。DiVeR随后利用这一信号对验证器进行重新加权（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: DiVeR通过采样动作表示的分散程度来识别对任务成败起关键作用的决策关键状态，并据此重新加权验证器的学习，从而更有效地实现VLA策略的测试时扩展。
en_tdlr: DiVeR identifies decision-critical states by measuring the dispersion of sampled action representations and uses this signal to reweight verifier learning, enabling more effective test-time scaling for VLA policies.
